vehicleUpdates.headline: Generous rear-facing clearance; three-across buckle compromise
vehicleUpdates.summary: Original Air RWD has strong longitudinal space. Three-across evidence is a related GT-Line test; an Air family review also favours two seats over three. Check the exact one-rear-facing / two-forward-facing-or-booster arrangement.

observedConsumption.basis: AAA MY2022 Air RWD, February 2022 build, 14,049 km: 93 km Geelong route, 24–28 April 2025, 17–25°C, damp/dry. Result 166 Wh/km = 16.6 kWh/100km. Annex IV measures mains recharge including charging losses; do not add losses again. Separate from 16.5 WLTP; one test, not a Queensland lifetime average.

observedRange.basis: AAA calculated real-world electric range for the same MY2022 Air RWD test, 24–28 April 2025; not a full 484 km depletion run. Separate from 528 km WLTP. Conditions and battery condition matter.

familyFit.summary: Related GT-Line fits two rear-facing restraints and a centre booster, with restricted buckle access. The requested one rear-facing plus two-seat/booster mix is not established; family-fit scoring is withheld.
familyFit.row2: Air manufacturer documents confirm two outer ISOFIX positions and three rear top tethers; no centre ISOFIX.
familyFit.testedSeats: BabyDrive GT-Line: InfaSecure Attain More and Achieve More rear-facing, Aspire More centre. This differs from your one-rear-facing / two-forward-facing-or-booster target.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Centre belt buckle was awkward in the related three-across test. ANCAP could not correctly install one selected booster in the centre, testing restraints individually.
familyFit.access: Air family test found easy child exit but awkward manual flush handles. Air lacks GT-Line remote parking; test loading in a narrow parking bay.
familyFit.ventilation: B-pillar second-row vents confirmed for Air in MY22 and MY24 manufacturer lists.

safety.applicability: Original Australian Air RWD is explicitly covered; all EV6 variants except GT. Current ANCAP page lists December 2028 expiry. A rating is not proof that any three restraints fit.

vehicleUpdates.servicing: 12 months/15,000 km. MY22/MY24 manuals: brake fluid every 24 months; first coolant change 210,000 km/120 months, then 30,000 km/24 months. Obtain the exact VIN schedule and quote; existing prepaid plans can transfer.
pros: Documented room ahead of rear-facing restraints; Air has a flat rear floor and rear vents.
AAA exact Air test: 16.6 kWh/100 km mains consumption and calculated 484 km range, separately labelled from WLTP.
Fast DC charging on suitable infrastructure; Air tyre costs have a current fitted retail anchor.
cons: Three-across evidence includes difficult middle buckle access; not a universal booster fit.
Air manual flush handles and manual tailgate add effort when carrying children or bags.
Inspect ICCU/12 V and recall records; a recall repair is free when applicable.
inspection: Trial all three restraints together and check every buckle with the children seated.
Confirm VIN, build date, service history, recall completion and remaining warranty.
Check VIN completion of REC-006238 ICCU software recall; request documentation for any associated repair.
Test both AC and DC charging and inspect the auxiliary-battery history.
Fit your one rear-facing and two forward-facing/booster seats simultaneously, then check front driver comfort and daily buckle reach.
Check brake-fluid service invoices and any prepaid-service balance; do not import an Ioniq 5 coolant schedule.
Confirm the original warranty-start date and any prior commercial/rideshare use. Obtain written ICCU-extension terms for this VIN.
gaps: Exact Air three-across trial using your one-rear-facing / two-forward-facing-or-booster seats remains unverified.
Manufacturer DC vehicle peak remains unverified; 350 kW is charger infrastructure. CarExpert observed 202 kW once, not a certified maximum.
No representative Australian out-of-pocket repair annual mean or Air-specific household insurance quote found.
Later 84 kWh facelift is outside this original 77.4 kWh entry.

priceUpdates.geography: Motorama Toyota Hillcrest, Queensland; private seller, Queensland; Cars4us Pinkenba, Queensland
priceUpdates.kilometres: 53–59,306 km; three distinct Queensland used Air RWD examples
priceUpdates.note: Three distinct Queensland original Air RWD asks, re-read 18 October 2026; not sold-price evidence. The 53 km Motorama used-labelled car is a nearly-new outlier. Cars4us stock 74400/VIN ending 211021 is one physical car across cross-posts; its page also warns additional dealer fees may apply. Ask each seller for an all-in quote and current availability. No 84 kWh facelift, GT-Line or GT is included.
priceUpdates.estimateBasis: Median of the included advertised amounts. The displayed low/high are only the included observations, not an estimated market range. Fee bases differ; the point is a provisional cash-budget anchor, not a fee-normalised valuation. Add the relevant duty/transfer/registration before comparing all-in totals.

observations.note: Stock P005132; seller labels USED despite only 53 km. Air RWD original CV body/build 2024. Do not treat as a typical high-mileage used example.

Private-used Air RWD MY24, original 77.4 kWh generation; asking price excludes government charges. Build year/model year differ; verify VIN. Active price page retrieved, not an auction or sold-price result.

Used Air RWD MY24, stock 74400, VIN ending 211021 (cross-posted Autotrader 15329952; counted once). Dealer pay-in-full price explicitly excludes government charges. 77.4 kWh original generation; dealer equipment prose is labelled AI-generated and is not specification evidence. Confirm current reservation/availability with dealer.

ownershipUpdates.serviceBasis: ESTIMATE A$350/year (A$250–450) for a used Air without a prepaid balance. Current Air/GT-Line prepaid plan: A$758/3, A$1,446/5, A$2,136/7 services including GST; five-plan averages A$289.20/service but a used 2022–24 car cannot newly enrol after eligibility. Original MY22/MY24 manuals include brake fluid every 24 months and first coolant 210,000 km/120 months, then 30,000 km/24 months. No Air-specific current pay-as-you-go dealer quote found; ageing/severe-use supplements may cost more. Excludes tyres and unscheduled repairs.

risks.title: ICCU / 12 V-charging recall
risks.detail: REC-006238 covers selected 2021–2024 VINs and supersedes REC-005946. Software-related ICCU failure can stop 12 V charging; Kia inspects and replaces hardware if required, plus updates software, free.
risks.priceBasis: Official VIN-applicable recall work is free. The separate paid ICCU scenario below applies only if recall, warranty, extended cover and other remedies do not cover the fault.
risks.warranty: Australian manufacturer statements reported by Drive in May 2026 describe 15-year/300,000-km ICCU cover from first registration for EV6 MY22–24. This is reported component cover, not a verified VIN-specific contract; obtain written eligibility and exclusions from the Australian dealer. Recall rectification remains free for affected VINs; use a paid stress case only when every applicable remedy is unavailable.

risks.title: Full traction-battery replacement — stress case
risks.detail: Budget for a complete pack only if diagnosis supports replacement. A module, control-system or drive-unit-only repair can be substantially cheaper; this range does not predict failure.
risks.priceBasis: ESTIMATE: model-specific Australian quote unavailable; based on the Insurance Council’s 2024 A$7,500–30,000 benchmark (itself converted from US research, not Australian installed invoices) and a broker’s A$10,000–30,000+ general guide, adjusted for the 77.4 kWh class and an explicit allowance above the generic upper benchmark. Full replacement planning total assumes parts, labour and GST; not a hard ceiling or a priced repair offer.
risks.warranty: Apply the original model-year terms; do not infer full battery replacement from a warning light.

risks.title: Brake pads and discs example — one axle
risks.detail: A paid brake job is separate from standard prepaid servicing. Inspect before budgeting: regenerative braking changes wear, but does not remove the need for sound friction brakes.
risks.priceBasis: ESTIMATE: EV6-specific quote unavailable; based on AutoGuru’s Australian A$500–700+ front pads/discs benchmark, widened for larger EV/OEM parts. Assumes one axle, parts, labour and GST; excludes tyres, calipers and unrelated repairs.
risks.warranty: Manufacturing cover excludes normal wear and external damage.

risks.title: ICCU hardware replacement if all cover is unavailable
risks.detail: Conditional paid stress case only: first confirm recall, original warranty, any ICCU extension and other remedies. This is not added as a routine annual cost and implies no failure probability.
risks.priceBasis: ESTIMATE: Australian model-specific quote unavailable; first-party US OEM ICCU listing is about US$1,658–2,445 for EV6. Illustrative US$1=A$1.50, plus 10% GST/import/parts variation and roughly A$800–2,000 diagnosis, labour, coolant/fuse allowance. Foreign part is a pricing proxy, not confirmed Australian-VIN fitment; not a live FX or installation quote.
risks.warranty: Australian manufacturer statements reported by Drive in May 2026 describe 15-year/300,000-km ICCU cover from first registration for EV6 MY22–24. This is reported component cover, not a verified VIN-specific contract; obtain written eligibility and exclusions from the Australian dealer. Recall rectification remains free for affected VINs; use a paid stress case only when every applicable remedy is unavailable.

risks.title: Other early EV6 VIN-specific campaigns
risks.detail: REC-005455 concerns selected 2021–2022 cars’ park-pawl/Shift Control Unit software (roll-away risk). REC-005939 concerns a defective driveshaft in selected 2023 EV6 VINs. Both provide free dealer remedies and are separate from ICCU campaigns.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 for the official VIN-applicable recall remedy. This is rectification of an identified campaign, not a future owner-paid replacement quote.
risks.warranty: Check the VIN and campaign completion with the Australian manufacturer; official recall rectification is separate from ordinary warranty expiry.

reviewUpdates.scope: ProductReview RWD Air page:4.0/5 from 2 contributions, one owner and one disclosed borrowed-car expert. Page groups 2022–2026/other-year aliases; contributions concern original Air. Tiny mixed sample, not an owner-only reliability survey.
reviewUpdates.summary: One owner and one expert praise the drive and charging but question original new-price equipment value. The expert misstates Air range/consumption using GT-Line figures; manufacturer and AAA figures take precedence.
positiveThemes: Enjoyable, quiet driving and adjustable regeneration.
negativeThemes: Equipment omissions and value against newer competitors.
Lane assistance and some cabin-material concerns.

expertReviews.scope: Exact original Air family test; historical new price and service offers are not current used-price evidence.
expertReviews.verdict: Comfortable and practical Air; narrow three-seat and manual-handle compromises.
positiveThemes: Comfortable ride and generous longitudinal cabin space.
Useful rear amenities and clear technology.
negativeThemes: Road noise at higher speed; three-across needs narrow seats.

insuranceUpdates.basis: Youi EV6 mean A$1,569, rounded to A$1,570, for comprehensive policies sold 22 November 2025–22 May 2026; published indicative band A$984–2,065. Model comparisons require at least ten policies, but the exact EV6 count is undisclosed. National mixed years, trims and customers; not a Queensland Air household quote. Dashboard A$980–3,500 sensitivity bounds are assumptions. Obtain a personal quote.

tyreUpdates.basis: Budget aftermarket fitted-set estimate, not a retailer quote. TyrePoint Nexen N-Fera SU1 105W is A$219 each / A$876 four fitted on sale, including GST/balance/disposal (A$240 regular each); A$900 is a rounded planning value. Possible SUV freight and local stock need a final quote. A 105W replacement-price reference, subject to the actual year/VIN placard. The former premium retail example did not establish the vehicle minimum. Life is a common 40,000 km planning assumption (25,000–60,000 km sensitivity), not a measured model or tyre average. Wear varies with tyre choice, driving, maintenance and vehicle; model-specific replacement averages were not verified. Annual allowance = set budget × annual km ÷ 40,000, rounded to A$10. Age/damage can require earlier replacement. Alignment is additional; actual placard, wheel package and local fitted quote must be checked. Matching size/load/speed does not establish equal braking, efficiency or durability.

repairReserveUpdates.basis: ESTIMATE A$1,000/year savings(A$550–1,900), retained: no credible Australian Air annual paid-failure average found. Original vehicle/HV cover and VIN-applicable free recall remedies reduce owner-paid exposure; reported 15 year/300,000 km ICCU extension still requires written Australian VIN eligibility. Reserve covers other uncovered ageing electrical/thermal/chassis faults, not recall work, routine fluids, tyres or insured crashes. No failure probability inferred from forum complaints or one foreign part price. A full traction pack is a separate conditional stress case.

fitAssessments.summary: Related GT-Line fits two rear-facing restraints and a centre booster, with restricted buckle access. The requested one rear-facing plus two-seat/booster mix is not established; family-fit scoring is withheld.

arrangement.detail: Published GT-Line trial and photo show two rear-facing InfaSecure convertibles plus a centre Aspire More booster. This differs from the requested one rear-facing plus two forward-facing seats or boosters. The Air review also favours two seats and says three require narrow restraints; no matched mixed trial was found.

buckles.detail: Related three-across centre buckle was difficult; ANCAP could not correctly install one selected centre booster individually. This is a documented restriction, not failure of every booster or a three-booster test.

space.detail: Related GT-Line fitted 186 cm front occupants ahead of rear-facing seats with room remaining. Exact Air review corroborates useful front clearance with a 0–4 rear-facing restraint and a flat rear floor; verify your driver position.

access.detail: Exact Air test reports easy child exit but awkward manually operated flush door handles. No quantified door-opening measurement or exact three-restraint loading trial; no third row.

audit.summary: Exact AAA Air observed energy/range added; original manuals verify coolant interval instead of importing Ioniq 5 costs. Family scoring now distinguishes rear-facing clearance from centre-buckle restriction. Current asks/premiums/tyres rechecked; unsupported repair annual mean remains a labelled estimate.

items.finding: Three distinct Queensland asks: A$40,000 excluding charges / 26,376 km; A$41,990 excluding charges / 59,306 km; A$48,980 drive-away / 53 km. Median A$41,990 retained. Different fee bases and the nearly-new outlier matter; Cars4us fees may be additional. These are asks, not transactions.

Original MY22/MY24 Air: 77.4 kWh, 528 km WLTP, 16.5 kWh/100km WLTP and 10.5 kW AC; CCS2 / Type 2. The 18-minute 10–80% claim uses a 350 kW charger, not a 350 kW vehicle peak. Added matched AAA results: 16.6 kWh/100km from mains recharge and 484 km calculated test range. GT-Line and later 84 kWh cars remain separate.

Air anchors and B-pillar vents verified. Related GT-Line fitted two rear-facing restraints and a centre booster tightly: 186 cm front-seat clearance was positive, centre-buckle access restricted. The Air review also reports generous front clearance but a constrained three-across fit. Your one rear-facing plus two-seat/booster arrangement remains pending. Boot: 490 L VDA. Facing-photo recheck: the requested one rear-facing plus two-seat/booster mix is not established, so no family-fit score is assigned.

Original private-use warranty: 7 years / unlimited km; high-voltage components and pre-MY27 70% capacity cover: 7 years / 150,000 km. Remaining cover transfers. Exceptions include 2 years for the 12 V battery, 3 years for the head unit and a 150,000 km commercial-use cap. Confirm reported ICCU extensions in writing for the VIN; overseas terms do not establish Australian eligibility.

12 months / 15,000 km; retained A$350/year used-car budget. The current A$1,446 five-plan offer applies to eligible new cars, not used pay-as-you-go servicing. MY22/MY24 brake fluid: 24 months; coolant first 210,000 km / 120 months, then 30,000 km / 24 months. Fitted fluid/dealer quotes remain unavailable.

Retained A$1,570 from Youi’s A$1,569 mean, November 2025–May 2026 cohort; published indicative band A$984–2,065. Exact sample size and Air subgroup unavailable. National mixed trims and customers; no household quote. Dashboard A$980–3,500 bounds are assumptions.

Budget aftermarket audit, 18 October 2026. 235/55R19 105W replacement reference: A$900 for four fitted. Common 40,000 km life is an illustrative assumption, not model-specific wear evidence. Prices and annual savings are estimates; check the real placard and local fitted quote.

Retained A$1,000 repair savings; no representative Australian annual paid-fault average found. ICCU, earlier parking and driveshaft recalls have free VIN-applicable remedies. Removed 2025 cluster campaign from the original MY22–24 Air list. Paid ICCU/battery stress cases remain low-confidence ranges, not failure forecasts.

Air 4.0/5 from two contributions retained, explicitly one owner plus a borrowed-car professional. That contributor also mixes GT-Line figures, so it cannot establish Air specifications. Added independent 2024 Air CarsGuide 7.9/10; CarExpert’s qualitative verdict stays separate. No large applicable Australian reliability survey found.

Maker limits: 1,600 kg braked towing / 100 kg towball. The 2022 ANCAP assessment explicitly covers Air and excludes GT; expiry December 2028. Restraint matrix tests individual positions. QLD private EV annual rego/CTP A$782.15–798.15, midpoint A$790.15. Duty below A$100,000 is A$2 per A$100, rounded up. Resale remains a scenario.
